transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I keep hearing voices at work, like through the call-light speaker and the hallway vents. They’re telling me which patient records have been changed, and it sounds clear—like someone is standing right next to me—even when the unit is quiet and nobody else hears it.
Besides hearing these voices, have you noticed any other unusual experiences, like seeing things that aren’t there or believing something is happening that others say isn’t?

I don’t really see things, no. But I do believe something is going on with the wound-care charts. There’s a pattern in them that management doesn’t want people noticing. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just late entries or coding mistakes, but I can tell they’re watching what I write now because I’m the one who caught it.
Do you believe that your interpretation of the wound-care charts is definitely accurate, even though your supervisor has told you it's just mistakes and coding errors?

Yes. I know what I’m seeing in those charts. It’s not just late entries or coding mistakes. There’s a pattern there, and management doesn’t want anyone noticing it. I can tell they’re watching what I write now because I’m the one who caught it.
Can you explain what you believe is happening with the wound-care charts and why you think management is watching what you write?

The wound-care charts keep showing the same kind of changes, like it’s not random mistakes. I know my supervisor says it’s late entries or coding errors, but that doesn’t explain the pattern I’m seeing.

And since I noticed it, it feels like management is paying attention to everything I write. Like they’re checking my notes because I’m the one who caught what’s happening.

Even though your supervisor has told you that the changes in the wound-care charts are just late entries or coding mistakes, do you still believe with certainty that there's a hidden pattern that management is trying to hide from others?

Yes. I know it’s a real pattern. I’ve looked at enough of those charts to know it’s not just random mistakes or late entries. My supervisor can say that, but it doesn’t change what I’m seeing. And since I noticed it, I can tell management is watching what I write, like they know I caught something they don’t want other people to see.

Even though your supervisor has explained that the changes in the wound-care charts are just mistakes or coding errors, do you believe your interpretation so strongly that you feel no doubt about it at all?

Yes. I don’t really have doubt about it. I know what those charts are showing, and it’s not just mistakes. My supervisor can call it coding errors or late entries, but I can see the pattern. And since I caught it, I can tell management is watching what I write.
Have you considered the possibility that your interpretation of the wound-care charts might be incorrect, even after your supervisor has explained it as coding errors or late entries?

I’ve thought about what my supervisor said, but no, I don’t really think I’m wrong about it. The charts show a pattern, and it doesn’t feel like late entries or coding mistakes to me. And after I noticed it, management started watching what I write because I’m the one who caught it.

Even though your supervisor has repeatedly told you that the changes in the wound-care charts are just coding errors or late entries, do you believe your interpretation so strongly that no amount of explanation or evidence would change your mind about it?

Yes. I mean, I know what my supervisor keeps saying, but it doesn’t change what I’ve seen. Those charts have a pattern, and management doesn’t want people noticing it. So no, I don’t think another explanation would change my mind, because I can tell they’re watching what I write since I caught it.
Can you think of any explanation or evidence that would make you doubt your belief about the wound-care charts and management monitoring your notes?

Honestly, no. I can’t think of anything that would make me doubt it right now. I know what I saw in those wound-care charts, and it’s a pattern they don’t want people to see. My supervisor can keep saying it’s late entries or coding mistakes, but that doesn’t explain all of it to me. And since I noticed it, I can tell management is watching what I write.
Have you ever thought that even if someone showed you proof that the wound-care charts were just coding errors or late entries, you still wouldn’t believe it?

Yes. I’ve thought that. Even if someone came in with paperwork saying it was just coding errors or late entries, I don’t think I’d believe that was the whole truth. I know what I saw in those charts. There’s a pattern there, and management doesn’t want it noticed. And since I’m the one who caught it, I can tell they’re watching what I write.
